# Mitigation Summary

## Action
Tune AWS WAFv2 managed rule group AWS-AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet on Web ACL CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4: add RuleActionOverrides switching three false-positive sub-rules — SizeRestrictions_BODY, NoUserAgent_HEADER, UserAgent_BadBots_HEADER — from Block to Count, leaving all other sub-rules and rule groups blocking.

## Reasoning
CommonRuleSet (Priority 3, OverrideAction None, no RuleActionOverrides) was the sole blocking rule during 17:32–18:25 UTC on CloudFront EEXAMPLE000001, false-positiving on legitimate large POST form bodies (SizeRestrictions_BODY) and legitimate automated/non-browser clients (NoUserAgent_HEADER / UserAgent_BadBots_HEADER). No WAF config change in ~17 days (CloudTrail), so the managed sub-rules are simply too aggressive for this app's legitimate traffic. The incident self-recovered when the triggering traffic subsided, but the false positives will recur on the next burst, so a forward-looking tuning is warranted. Count mode removes the false positives while preserving the rest of CommonRuleSet and the AntiDDoS, IP Reputation, rate-based, KnownBadInputs, and SQLi rule groups.

**Purpose:** Snapshot the complete current Web ACL (all six rules, DefaultAction, VisibilityConfig, OnSourceDDoSProtectionConfig) so the exact pre-change state can be restored during rollback.
**Advisory:** Verify the backup is for CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 (Id f0598f76-f04d-456a-beff-5521b48914d4, CLOUDFRONT scope) before relying on it.

### Step 2: Pre Validate

#### 2.1 Obtain a fresh LockToken and confirm the CommonRuleSet rule still has…
**Type:** command
```
aws wafv2 get-web-acl --scope CLOUDFRONT --region us-east-1 --id f0598f76-f04d-456a-beff-5521b48914d4 --name CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 --query '{LockToken:LockToken,CommonRuleSet:WebACL.Rules[?Name==`AWS-AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet`]}'
```
**Purpose:** Obtain a fresh LockToken and confirm the CommonRuleSet rule still has OverrideAction None and no RuleActionOverrides before modifying. UpdateWebACL rejects a stale LockToken (WAFOptimisticLockException).
**Advisory:** Use the LockToken captured here — not the earlier 36528525-b4de-4ef9-acfc-17bebab7891f — in the apply step.

### Step 3: Apply

#### 3.1 Add RuleActionOverrides (ActionToUse=Count) for SizeRestrictions_BODY…
**Type:** command
```
aws wafv2 update-web-acl --scope CLOUDFRONT --region us-east-1 --id f0598f76-f04d-456a-beff-5521b48914d4 --name CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 --lock-token <FRESH_LOCKTOKEN_FROM_PRE_VALIDATE> --default-action Allow={} --visibility-config SampledRequestsEnabled=true,CloudWatchMetricsEnabled=true,MetricName=CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 --rules file://rules.json
```
**Purpose:** Add RuleActionOverrides (ActionToUse=Count) for SizeRestrictions_BODY, NoUserAgent_HEADER, UserAgent_BadBots_HEADER on the Priority 3 CommonRuleSet rule so legitimate large forms and automated clients are no longer blocked. UpdateWebACL REPLACES the whole ruleset — build rules.json from the backup resending ALL six rules, modifying only CommonRuleSet, and carry over OnSourceDDoSProtectionConfig.
**Risks:** Omitting any of the other five rules DELETES them — removing AntiDDoS, IP reputation, rate-limiting, KnownBadInputs, or SQLi protection. Always resend the complete ruleset from the backup., Count (not Block) means genuinely malicious requests matching these three sub-rules are allowed and only counted — a deliberate, scoped coverage reduction limited to the three sub-rules; the rest keep blocking.
**Advisory:** Count keeps these sub-rules observable via CountedRequests and sampled requests for later refinement (e.g. a scope-down excluding only legitimate paths).

### Step 4: Post Validate

#### 4.1 Verify the three RuleActionOverrides are applied (each set to Count)…
**Type:** command
```
aws wafv2 get-web-acl --scope CLOUDFRONT --region us-east-1 --id f0598f76-f04d-456a-beff-5521b48914d4 --name CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 --query 'WebACL.Rules[?Name==`AWS-AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet`].Statement.ManagedRuleGroupStatement.RuleActionOverrides'
```
**Purpose:** Verify the three RuleActionOverrides are applied (each set to Count) and all six rules are still present and unchanged.

#### 4.2 Monitor CommonRuleSet BlockedRequests after the change to confirm…
**Type:** command
```
aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace AWS/WAFV2 --metric-name BlockedRequests --region us-east-1 --dimensions Name=WebACL,Value=CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 Name=Rule,Value=AWS-AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet --start-time <NOW_MINUS_30_MIN> --end-time <NOW> --period 300 --statistics Sum
```
**Purpose:** Monitor CommonRuleSet BlockedRequests after the change to confirm false-positive blocks on legitimate traffic have stopped (the three sub-rules now surface as CountedRequests).
**Advisory:** The incident self-recovered, so blocks may already read zero; decisive confirmation is the next large-form/automated burst no longer producing 403.

### Step 5: Rollback

#### 5.1 Obtain a fresh LockToken before restoring the pre-change backup
**Type:** command
```
aws wafv2 get-web-acl --scope CLOUDFRONT --region us-east-1 --id f0598f76-f04d-456a-beff-5521b48914d4 --name CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 --query LockToken --output text
```
**Purpose:** Obtain a fresh LockToken before restoring the pre-change backup.

#### 5.2 Revert to the original CommonRuleSet default-Block behavior by…
**Type:** command
```
aws wafv2 update-web-acl --scope CLOUDFRONT --region us-east-1 --id f0598f76-f04d-456a-beff-5521b48914d4 --name CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 --lock-token <FRESH_LOCKTOKEN> --default-action Allow={} --visibility-config SampledRequestsEnabled=true,CloudWatchMetricsEnabled=true,MetricName=CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 --rules file://webacl-backup-20261006-rules.json
```
**Purpose:** Revert to the original CommonRuleSet default-Block behavior by resending the exact pre-change ruleset from the prepare backup (RuleActionOverrides removed), restoring SizeRestrictions_BODY, NoUserAgent_HEADER, UserAgent_BadBots_HEADER to Block.
**Risks:** Rolling back reinstates the false positives that caused the incident; use only if Count mode produces an unacceptable security impact, and pair it with a narrower scope-down approach.

## Code Change Specification

### Requirements

#### 1. Codify the CommonRuleSet sub-rule tuning in the IaC definition of Web ACL CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 so the fix survives redeployment and drift.
**Description:** The Web ACL was auto-created by the CloudFront WAF integration; if reconciled from IaC (CDK/CloudFormation/Terraform) or re-created by the console WAF toggle, a manual RuleActionOverrides change will be lost and the false positives will return. In the source definition, add RuleActionOverrides to the AWS-AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet statement setting SizeRestrictions_BODY, NoUserAgent_HEADER, UserAgent_BadBots_HEADER to Count, leaving all else unchanged. Stronger follow-up: replace the blanket Count override with scope-down statements excluding only the legitimate form-submission paths and known automated-client identities.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- IaC for CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 sets SizeRestrictions_BODY, NoUserAgent_HEADER, UserAgent_BadBots_HEADER in AWS-AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet to Count via RuleActionOverrides.
- A redeploy from source yields a live Web ACL matching the mitigation (verified with get-web-acl) with no drift.
- All other CommonRuleSet sub-rules and the AntiDDoS, RateBasedRule-IP-300, AmazonIpReputationList, KnownBadInputsRuleSet, SQLiRuleSet rules remain unchanged.
- Legitimate large-form submissions and automated clients to EEXAMPLE000001 no longer receive 403 attributable to these three sub-rules.

# Investigation Summary

## Symptoms

### Customers could not submit forms (HTTP 403)
**Description:** During 2026-10-06 17:32–17:52 and again 18:05–18:25 UTC, legitimate checkout form submissions (POST /checkout, ~10KB bodies) to CloudFront EEXAMPLE000001 received HTTP 403. ~1,200 such requests blocked, from a real desktop Chrome browser (198.51.100.80).
**Time:** 2026-10-06T17:32:10Z - 2026-10-06T18:25:46Z

### Automated clients received HTTP 403
**Description:** During the same window, legitimate automated/non-browser GET requests to /home and /catalog on CloudFront EEXAMPLE000001 received HTTP 403. ~599 such requests blocked, from a UA-less automated client (198.51.100.70).
**Time:** 2026-10-06T17:32:10Z - 2026-10-06T18:25:46Z

## Findings

### Root Cause: CommonRuleSet managed-rule defaults mismatch the app's legitimate traffic
**Description:** Fundamental cause of the 2026-10-06 17:30–18:30 UTC 403s. The WAF configuration was STATIC — CloudTrail shows no change to Web ACL CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 (nor any mutative WAFv2 event) in ~17 days, so this was NOT a config change, deployment, or rollback. The deepest cause is a mismatch between the always-on AWS-managed AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet default sub-rule behavior and this application's legitimate traffic characteristics: (1) checkout form POSTs carry bodies >8KB, exceeding the CRS SizeRestrictions_BODY default limit, and (2) legitimate non-browser/automated clients send requests the CRS User-Agent sub-rules (NoUserAgent_HEADER / UserAgent_BadBots_HEADER) target. When a burst of such legitimate-but-unusual traffic arrived during 17:32–18:25 (an inputs/traffic-shape trigger, not a change), these managed sub-rules produced false-positive 403s, then stopped on their own at ~18:25 when the traffic subsided — hence the self-recovery with no operator action. It WILL recur whenever similar legitimate traffic arrives again until the sub-rules are tuned (hence the mitigation to set them to Count via RuleActionOverrides and codify in IaC).
**Cascades to:** symptom-automated-403, symptom-form-403

#### Gaps
- **Phase 2 terminating sub-rule not confirmed at the record level:** The Phase 2 (≈18:05–18:25 UTC) BLOCK records' ruleGroupList terminatingRule.ruleId was not read directly by the dedicated confirmation tasks: S3 Select (select_object_content) returns MethodNotAllowed on bucket aws-waf-logs-012345678901_1, the Phase 2 log objects decompress beyond the 200k-token context ceiling (so get_object/distill overflow), and no CloudWatch Logs fallback exists for this Web ACL. The Phase 2 sub-rule is nonetheless strongly supported — attributed to NoUserAgent_HEADER by the first waf-logs task's Athena query (599 blocks, GET /home + /catalog, client 198.51.100.70), corroborated by per-rule WAF metric block labels (NoUserAgent_Header / BadBots_Header) and the captured in-window Artillery automated-client fingerprint. Closing the record-level gap would require an Athena query (WHERE action='BLOCK') over the Phase 2 partitions.

### Hypothesis: CommonRuleSet is the sole blocking rule — managed-rule false positive on load-test traffic
**Description:** Per-rule WAFV2 BlockedRequests show AWS-AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet was the ONLY rule that blocked during the window; AntiDDoS, AmazonIpReputationList, KnownBadInputs, and SQLi all blocked zero, and the rate-based rule was COUNT only. This rules out the earlier multi-rule/SQLi hypothesis — both symptom groups trace to CommonRuleSet. Blocking came in two humps (~60/min 17:32–17:52, gap, ~30/min 18:05–18:25, ~1,300 total) matching the two CloudFront 4xx bumps. No UpdateWebACL occurred (ACL static), so this was not a config change; WAF logs show load-test traffic (Artillery user-agent, single client IP), suggesting a synthetic traffic burst tripped CommonRuleSet. Sub-rule attribution (which CommonRuleSet sub-rules terminated each symptom group) is still pending.
**Cascades to:** symptom-form-403, symptom-automated-403

The Phase 2 sub-rule is nonetheless strongly supported — attributed to NoUserAgent_HEADER by the first waf-logs task's Athena query (599 blocks, GET /home + /catalog, client 198.51.100.70), corroborated by per-rule WAF metric block labels (NoUserAgent_Header / BadBots_Header) and the captured in-window Artillery automated-client fingerprint. {"id": "7e6206d2-3db1-4e5a-bd5c-7459a4215af4", "role": "user", "content": [{"text": "IMPORTANT: Respond entirely in English (observations, findings, summaries). Technical terms, resource names, and ARNs stay in their original form.

CONTEXT: We are investigating 403 responses on CloudFront distribution EEXAMPLE000001 (domain d111111abcdef8.cloudfront.net) between 2026-10-06 17:30 and 18:30 UTC. Two symptoms: (1) some customers could not submit forms, (2) some automated clients received 403. The distribution has an AWS WAF (WAFv2) Web ACL attached named "CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4" (CLOUDFRONT scope, global). WAF is the prime suspect for the 403s.

AWS account: 012345678901_1. WAFv2 CloudFront-scope metrics live in the CloudWatch namespace "AWS/WAFV2" in region us-east-1, with dimensions WebACL="CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4" and Region="Global", plus a per-rule dimension "Rule".

The Web ACL rules (by Rule dimension value / MetricName) are:
- AWS-AWSManagedRulesAntiDDoSRuleSet
- AWS-RateBasedRule-IP-300-CreatedByCloudFront
- AWS-AWSManagedRulesAmazonIpReputationList
- AWS-AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet
- AWS-AWSManagedRulesKnownBadInputsRuleSet
- AWS-AWSManagedRulesSQLiRuleSet
